title: Watch any Terabox link in your browser with the Terabox Player
summary: Paste a Terabox share link, press Watch, and the video plays right on the videos page: no app, no download, and the same player controls you use for everything else.
author: Quillwood Team
imageCaption: The Terabox Player: paste a share link and press Watch.
body: Terabox share links usually send you to an app or a download page. The Terabox Player skips both. Paste the link on the videos page and the video plays in your browser, in the same player as every other video here.

body.h: How to watch a Terabox link

body: Open the Terabox Player from the header, or the Terabox tab on the videos page. Copy the share link from Terabox’s Share button, then paste it into the box. On a phone, the Paste button next to the box fills it in from your clipboard in one tap.

Press Watch. The player asks Terabox for the video’s streams, which can take up to a minute for a large file. When it’s ready the video starts at the top of the page, with its title and a “From Terabox” label under it.

body.h: The full player, not a preview

body: A Terabox video gets everything the regular player has: quality from Auto up to the best stream Terabox offers, playback speed, picture-in-picture, fullscreen, keyboard shortcuts and resume where you left off.

body.quote: Paste, press Watch, and it plays. That’s the whole idea.

body: Under the video there’s a Watch new video box, so you can paste the next link without going back. Beside the player, Up next lists Terabox videos that are already saved on the site; tap one and it opens the same way.
The Terabox Player is part of Member Lite and Member Pro. If you’re not signed in, the videos page asks you to sign in first, then plays the link you pasted.

title: Which Terabox links work? Share links, mirror sites and common errors
summary: The player accepts share links from terabox.com and its many mirror domains. Here’s what a good link looks like and what each error message means.
author: Support Team
imageCaption: A Terabox share link: the part after /s/1 is the share’s id.
body: The Terabox Player plays share links: the links Terabox gives you when you press Share on a file. A good one looks like terabox.com/s/1abc… or has ?surl= in it.

Terabox serves the same shares from many addresses, and the player knows them all: terabox.com, terabox.app, teraboxapp.com, teraboxlink.com, 1024tera.com, 1024terabox.com, terasharelink.com, terafileshare.com, freeterabox.com, 4funbox.com, mirrobox.com, nephobox.com and more. You can paste the link with or without https:// in front.
“That isn’t a Terabox link” means the address isn’t on a Terabox domain. Check that you copied the share link and not a page that links to it.
“This Terabox link has no share in it” means the link points at Terabox but not at a shared file. Open the file in Terabox, press Share, and copy that link instead.
“This Terabox link has no video to play” means the share opened but holds no video file, for example a folder of photos.
“Terabox videos are busy right now” means Terabox is limiting requests. Try again in a few hours. “Couldn’t reach Terabox” is usually your connection: check it and press Watch again.
If you’ve been signed out, you’ll see “Your session has ended”. Sign in again with your account number and paste the link once more.

title: Terabox Videos: a ready-made list to start watching from
summary: No link to hand? The Terabox tab now lists videos that are already saved on the site, page by page, each one a tap away.
author: Quillwood Team
imageCaption: Saved Terabox videos, with thumbnails and durations.
body: Below the paste box on the Terabox tab there’s now a list called Terabox Videos. Every card shows the video’s thumbnail, its length and when it was added.
Tap a card and it opens exactly like a pasted link: the player fetches fresh streams from Terabox and the video starts at the top of the page.
The list is split into pages, with a pager at the bottom. The page you were on stays visible while the next one loads, so the cards don’t jump around.
While a saved video plays, the next six saved videos sit beside it as Up next, and the full list continues underneath, so you can keep going without leaving the player.

title: A tour of the videos page
summary: Everything on the videos page in one place: the video grid, search, channels, Shorts, the Terabox tab and your account menu.
author: Quillwood Team
imageCaption: The videos page on a laptop, with the tabs along the top.
body: The videos page is the heart of Quillwood. Once you’re signed in as Member Lite or Member Pro, it’s also your home page: opening the site takes you straight there. The blog you’re reading stays one tap away.
Videos are listed newest first, 40 to a page, with a pager at the bottom. Each card shows the thumbnail, length, channel and views. Tap one to open its watch page.
The search box at the top searches every video, not just the page you’re on. Channel chips under it narrow the grid to one channel, and the Channels tab shows every channel at once.
A shelf of Shorts sits near the top of the home grid; tap one to open the full-screen Shorts feed. The Terabox tab is where you paste a Terabox link or pick one of the saved Terabox videos.
On a phone the tabs move to a bar at the bottom of the screen: Home, Terabox, Search and Profile. The search box takes over the top bar while you type, and the profile tab opens your account menu.

title: Find any video with search and channel chips
summary: Type a few words or tap a channel: the grid updates as you go, and the address bar keeps your filter so Back undoes it.
author: Support Team
imageCaption: Channel chips under the search box.
body: Start typing in the search box and the grid updates a moment after you stop. The search covers every video on the site, and results come back 40 at a time, like the main grid.
The chips under the search box are channels. Tap one and you see only that channel’s videos; tap All to go back. Search and a channel work together, so you can look for a title inside one channel.
The Channels tab lists every channel. Picking one there opens the home grid already filtered to it.
A channel filter lives in the address, so you can bookmark a channel or send it to a friend. Pressing Back takes the filter off again.

title: Series, episodes and Up next
summary: A video with episodes shows them under the player and inside it, counts down to the next one, and remembers which episode you were on.
author: Player Team
imageCaption: The episodes row inside the player, available in fullscreen.
body: Some videos come in parts. When a video has episodes, they’re listed as numbered cards under the player, and the one playing is marked.

The Episodes button in the player controls opens a row of episode cards over the video. It works in fullscreen, so you can switch episode without leaving it. Picking one switches in place and keeps fullscreen on.
When an episode ends, a short countdown starts for the next one. Let it run, or press play on it straight away.
The episode you’re on is part of the page’s address, so a reload or a shared link opens the same episode. The video title shows the episode number too.
When a video has no more episodes, Up next takes over with related videos from the same site.

title: Comments: post, like and sort
summary: Signed-in viewers can comment under any video, like other comments, sort by Top or Newest and delete their own.
author: Support Team
imageCaption: The comments section under a video.
body: Under every video there’s a comments section. Sign in and the box at the top is yours to write in.
Tap the thumb on a comment to like it. Sort by Top to see the most-liked comments first, or by Newest to follow the conversation as it happens.
You can delete any comment you wrote from its menu.

title: Shorts: swipe through quick videos
summary: Shorts are short vertical videos in a feed of their own. Swipe up for the next one, tap for sound, and share any short with its own link.
author: Quillwood Team
imageCaption: The Shorts feed on a phone.
body: Shorts are quick vertical videos. They appear as a shelf near the top of the videos page; tap one and the full Shorts feed opens on it.
Swipe up for the next short and down for the one before. Each short plays when it fills the screen and pauses when you move on.
Shorts start muted, because browsers don’t allow sound until you’ve tapped the page. Tap the speaker once and sound stays on for the rest of the feed.
Use the arrow keys or Page Up and Page Down to move between shorts, and M to mute or unmute.
Every short has its own address, so the link in your address bar opens that exact short for whoever you send it to.

title: Shorts load faster, and new ones show up straight away
summary: Shorts are now served from the same server as every other video, so the shelf fills quickly and new shorts appear as soon as they’re published.
author: Quillwood Team
imageCaption: The Shorts shelf on the videos page.
body: Until now the Shorts shelf was put together from a fixed list. Shorts now come from the video server, like the rest of the catalogue.
That means a new short is on the shelf as soon as the team publishes it, without waiting for the next release of the site.
The shelf is kept for a few minutes as you move around the videos page, so going back to Home doesn’t make it load again.

title: Inside the settings menu: quality, speed, audio and subtitles
summary: The gear button in the player holds quality, playback speed, audio tracks, subtitles, a link to the current moment and stats for nerds.
author: Player Team
imageCaption: The player’s settings menu, open over a video.
body: Press the gear in the player’s controls to open its settings. What’s in the menu depends on the video.
Auto picks the best quality your connection can keep playing smoothly, and changes it as your connection changes. Pick a fixed quality, such as 720p, to hold it there.
Speed goes from a quarter speed up to double. Videos with more than one audio track list them under Audio. Subtitles lists every language the video has; turn them on or off with C on a keyboard.
This copies a link that opens the video at the moment you’re watching, handy for showing someone exactly the bit you mean.
Shows the stream’s format, resolution, bitrate and buffer. Useful if a video stutters and you want to see why.

title: Every keyboard shortcut in the player
summary: Play, skip, change volume, go fullscreen and step frame by frame without touching the mouse. Press ? in the player to see them all.
author: Player Team
imageCaption: The shortcuts card, opened with the ? key.
body: The player works from the keyboard. You don’t need to remember all of this: press ? while a video is open and the list appears over it.
Space or K plays and pauses. J and L jump back or forward 10 seconds; the left and right arrows jump 5. The number keys 0 to 9 jump to that tenth of the video, so 5 is halfway.
The up and down arrows change the volume and M mutes. F goes fullscreen, I opens picture-in-picture and C turns subtitles on or off.
The < and > keys slow down or speed up playback. While paused, , and . step one frame back or forward. Home and End jump to the start and end; on a live stream, End takes you back to live.
Escape closes any menu that’s open.

title: Pick up where you left off, and share the exact moment
summary: The player remembers how far you got in each video, and a link can open a video at any second you choose.
author: Player Team
imageCaption: Resuming a video part-way through.
body: Close a video half-way through and come back later: it starts where you stopped. This works per video, so you can have several on the go at once.
Add t= and a number of seconds to a video’s address to open it at that point. The easiest way is Copy link at current time in the settings menu, which builds the link for you.
The player also remembers your volume between videos, so you don’t have to turn it down every time.

title: Picture-in-picture, fullscreen and double-tap to skip
summary: Keep a video playing in a small window while you do something else, and skip on a phone with a double tap.
author: Player Team
imageCaption: A video in a picture-in-picture window.
body: Picture-in-picture pops the video out into a small window that stays on top while you use other tabs or apps. Use the button in the controls or press I.
The fullscreen button, F or a double-click on the video fill the screen. Episodes and the settings menu work in fullscreen too.
Double-tap the right side of the video to skip forward and the left side to go back. Tap once to show or hide the controls.

title: The stream player plays HLS, DASH, MP4 and more
summary: The same player is also a page of its own at /player/: paste any stream address and it picks the right engine for it.
author: Player Team
imageCaption: The stream player with a pasted HLS link.
body: The player behind the videos page also has a page of its own at /player/. Paste the address of a live or on-demand stream and it plays in your browser.
HLS (.m3u8) and MPEG-DASH (.mpd), live or on demand; FLV and MPEG-TS; and anything the browser plays by itself, such as MP4, WebM, MOV and audio files.
If a link has no file extension, the player tries the browser first, then HLS, then DASH, until one works.
Live streams show a live button and let you scrub back through the part of the stream that’s still available. Press the button, or End, to return to live.
The stream’s server has to allow playback from other sites. RTMP and RTSP streams can’t play in a browser.

title: Member, Member Lite or Member Pro: which plan is yours?
summary: Three plans, one account number. Here’s what each one includes, how you get it, and how to move up.
author: Support Team
imageCaption: The three plans side by side.
body: Every Quillwood account is one of three plans. You can see yours in the account menu at the top right.

You get Member when you register on the blog directly. It covers the blog: guides, updates and comments. Videos aren’t included, but the Upgrade button next to your name adds them: pick Member Lite or Member Pro, pass one quick security check on the videos site, and you’re straight back here with videos.

You get Member Lite free when you register by pressing play on a video on the videos site. A Member who signs in from there becomes Member Lite too. It includes every video, Shorts and the Terabox Player, with ads.
Member Pro is everything in Lite without the ads, plus special videos for Pro members, early access to new videos and priority support. Get it from the Upgrade button on the videos page.

body.quote: Lite to watch for free, Pro to watch without ads.

title: Member Pro: no ads, special videos and early access
summary: Pay $5.00 once and Pro is yours for life. Shorter passes are there too: $0.50 for a week or $1.00 for a month.
author: Quillwood Team
imageCaption: The Upgrade to Pro dialog.
body: Member Pro takes the ads off every video and every page, and opens up videos made only for Pro members.
No ads. Special videos for Pro members. Early access to new videos before everyone else. Priority support when something goes wrong. And search by image, as soon as it opens.
Lifetime is the best value: $5.00, paid once, and Pro stays on for good, with no renewals to remember. If you’d like to try it first, one week is $0.50 and one month is $1.00.

Press Upgrade in the videos page’s top bar or account menu and pick a plan. After you pay you come back to the videos page, which confirms the payment and switches your account to Pro, usually within a few seconds.

title: Why Member Lite asks you to turn off your ad blocker
summary: Ads are what keep Member Lite free. If an ad blocker is on, the videos page asks you to turn it off or switch to Pro.
author: Support Team
imageCaption: The ad blocker notice on the videos page.
body: Member Lite is free because it shows ads. When the videos page sees that ads are being blocked, it shows a notice instead of the videos.
Turn off your ad blocker for this site, or pause it, and reload the page. The videos come back straight away.
If you’d rather not see ads at all, Member Pro is ad-free and never shows this notice.
Pro accounts aren’t checked. If you’ve just paid for Pro, the notice stays away while the payment is being confirmed.

title: Create your free account in under a minute
summary: All it takes is your name and a quick captcha. You get an account number, which is your login, so save it before you close the window.
author: Support Team
imageCaption: The account number, shown once after registering.
body: Creating an account takes two things: your full name and a quick captcha to show you’re a person. There’s no email and no password.
When you register, you get a 16-character account number in four groups, like xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx. It’s shown once. Copy it and keep it somewhere safe: it’s the only way to sign in.

Register on the blog and you’re a Member; press Upgrade next to your name any time to add videos. Register by pressing play on a video on the videos site and you’re Member Lite, which includes videos, from the start. See the plans guide for the details.

title: Your account number is your login: how to keep it safe
summary: Signing in takes your account number and a captcha. Treat the number like a password: anyone who has it can use your account.
author: Support Team
imageCaption: The sign-in box with an account number.
body: To sign in, press Sign in, type your account number and complete the captcha. That’s it.
Your account number works like a password. Save it in a password manager or a note only you can open, and don’t paste it into chats or comments.

You stay signed in on this browser. Each time you open the site it checks your account with the server, which keeps your session fresh and picks up plan changes, like an upgrade to Pro. If your session has ended, you’re signed out and can sign in again with your number.

title: From the videos site to playing in one tap
summary: Press play on any video on the videos site and it opens here, with a short sign-up in front of it. Once you’re in, the video starts.
author: Quillwood Team
imageCaption: Signing up over the video you chose.
body: The videos site is where you browse. Pressing play on a video there opens it on the videos page here, in a new tab.

If you don’t have an account yet, a short register box sits over the video you picked. Enter your name, pass the captcha, save your account number, and the video plays. Your new account is Member Lite.
Sign in from that same box. A Member who signs in this way is upgraded to Member Lite, so the video plays straight away.
The access you bring from the videos site lasts 12 hours, so there’s plenty of time to finish signing up.

title: What’s new: a Terabox videos list, faster Shorts and a Terabox Player page
summary: This release adds a list of saved Terabox videos, serves Shorts from the video server, and gives the Terabox Player its own page on the blog.
author: Quillwood Team
imageCaption: This week’s release.
body: Here’s what changed this week.

The Terabox tab now lists saved Terabox videos under the paste box, with pages and Up next. The Terabox Player also has its own page on the blog, linked from the header, where you can paste a link and go straight to watching it.
Shorts now come from the video server, so new ones appear as soon as they’re published.
The team can now add, edit and remove saved Terabox videos, and import a batch of them at once, without a new release of the site.

title: Coming soon to Member Pro: search with an image
summary: The search box already has an image option: upload, drop or paste a picture to find videos that match it. Results switch on soon.
author: Quillwood Team
imageCaption: The image option in the search box.
body: Sometimes you don’t know a video’s name, just what it looks like. Image search is for that.
Open the image option in the search box, then upload a picture, drag one in or paste one from your clipboard. Images up to 10 MB work. The videos that best match it come back, best match first.
The search box part is already on the videos page. Matching is being connected now; until it is, an image search tells you results aren’t ready yet. It will be part of Member Pro.

title: Member Lite and Pro now open straight to the videos page
summary: If your plan includes videos, opening the site takes you to them. The blog is still a tap away.
author: Quillwood Team
imageCaption: Signing in and landing on the videos page.
body: Most people with Member Lite or Member Pro come here to watch. So now, when you open the site with one of those plans, you land on the videos page instead of the blog.
The blog hasn’t gone anywhere. Use the account menu or go to /note/ to read the latest guides and updates.
Members without videos in their plan still see the blog first, with a short explanation of how to get videos if they open the videos page.
